decode.description: Whether the shape and assembly envelopes are rebuilt into live CAD geometry before the implementation sees them. Set to false by an implementation that needs the assembly tree's structure rather than the single compound it decodes to (the built-in URDF exporter is the one that does)

unless.description: The conditions this declaration does not work under. A list of clauses, any one of which excludes it (OR); a clause is a single tag, or a list of tags that must all hold together (AND) - e.g. [[arm, useDocker, useDockerKicad]]. It is skipped, with an INFO line saying so, wherever a clause holds. A tag names something true of the context: the host's architecture ('arm64', 'arm', 'x86_64'), its operating system ('linux', 'macos', 'windows'), that system's version ('ubuntu-24.04', 'macos-26'), a boolean configuration option in one of its two spellings ('useDocker' when on, '!useDocker' when off; likewise 'useDockerPython' and 'useDockerKicad'), or a tag the user configuration adds. '!' is part of a tag's name, not an operator.

file-hash.description: The hash of the file this declaration points at, as '<algorithm>:<digest>' -- md5, sha1, sha256 or sha512 (a bare digest is accepted too, and the algorithm is read from its length). It pins the *bytes*: a file fetched with 'fileFrom' is whatever the remote serves at the moment it is fetched, and the download is refused unless it hashes to this. Optional, but an object fetched without one is not reproducible and so fails the manufacturing test. Nothing to do with the hashes PartCAD computes for itself, such as a shape's cache key.

software-refs.description: The software objects an object ships with: a firmware image the board runs, a binary that has to be on the host. Optional, and most objects declare none. Each entry names a 'software' object, either of this package or of another ('<package path>:<name>'); a single one may be written on its own instead of as a list. Listed in the bill of materials of every assembly the object ends up in, and required to be obtainable by the manufacturing test.

shape-properties.description: What the shape this object produces reports about itself, as opposed to 'parameters', which are what is asked of the object type that produces it. Every entry here is an output: it describes the instantiated shape, and an exporter that has a way to state one writes it out rather than recomputing or losing it.

material.description: The name of the material this shape is made of.

color.description: The colour of this shape, as #RRGGBB or #RRGGBBAA.

physics.description: Physical properties, each with a documented name and unit. Lengths are millimetres and angles are degrees, as everywhere else in PartCAD; everything else is SI. A property that has no entry here is not carried: a format that states one PartCAD does not support fails the import, and a property PartCAD holds that the target format cannot state is reported on export.

centerOfMass.description: Centre of mass in the shape's own frame, in millimetres.

inertiaOrientation.description: Orientation of the frame the inertia tensor is stated in, as roll/pitch/yaw in degrees. Absent means aligned with the shape's own frame.

inertia.description: The inertia tensor about 'centerOfMass', in kg*m^2.

friction.description: Coefficient of friction, along the first friction direction.

friction2.description: Coefficient of friction, along the second friction direction.

frictionDirection.description: The first friction direction, in the shape's own frame.

minContactDepth.description: Penetration allowed before a contact force is applied, in millimetres.

maxContactVelocity.description: The largest velocity a contact correction may impart, in mm/s.

restitution.description: Coefficient of restitution: 0 is a dead stop, 1 is a perfect bounce.

maxContacts.description: The largest number of contact points to resolve at once.

velocityDamping.description: Velocity damping applied to the body itself.

selfCollide.description: Whether this body collides with the others of the same model.

gravity.description: Whether gravity acts on this body.

maxEffort.description: The largest effort a connection may exert: N*m for a turn, N for a move.

maxVelocity.description: The largest velocity a connection allows: deg/s for a turn, mm/s for a move.

damping.description: Damping resisting the movement a connection allows.

springStiffness.description: Stiffness of a spring returning a connection to 'springReference'.

springReference.description: The position a spring returns a connection to: degrees for a turn, millimetres for a move.

stopCfm.description: Constraint force mixing used at a connection's limits.

stopErp.description: Error reduction used at a connection's limits.

fudgeFactor.description: Solver scaling applied to a connection, between 0 and 1.

implicitSpringDamper.description: Whether the spring and damper are applied implicitly by the solver.

provideFeedback.description: Whether the simulator reports the forces at this connection.

shape-physics.description: The physical properties a shape may state about itself: 'physics' without the ones that describe a connection rather than a body. An effort limit, a joint damping or a spring belongs to the interface a connection is made through, not to the part that connection moves, so a part that states one has made a mistake rather than said something to carry. Stated as the whole vocabulary minus the connection-only names, so that a body property added to 'physics' is available here without being written down twice, and so that the two lists cannot drift apart.

not.description: The properties of a connection, which only an interface may state. See 'motion' and 'physics' on an interface.

motion.description: The freedom of movement a connection allows. Angles are degrees and lengths millimetres, as everywhere else in PartCAD.

axis.description: The axis moved about or along, in the frame of this interface's port.

limits.description: How far the movement may go: degrees for a turn, millimetres for a move.

softLimits.description: Limits a controller enforces before the hard ones, and the gains it does it with.

mimic.description: A movement that follows another one: value = multiplier * other + offset.

hold.description: The interface, or the list of interfaces, to hold this object by while it is connected to another one. The default for 'holdWith'/'holdTo' in the 'how' section of an ASSY 'connect*' node.

holdInstance.description: The instance of each interface listed in 'hold' to hold this object by, in the same order. The default for 'holdWithInstance'/'holdToInstance' in the 'how' section of an ASSY 'connect*' node.

holdForce.description: A force to hold this object with, in N. The default for the 'holdWithForce*'/'holdToForce*' fields in the 'how' section of an ASSY 'connect*' node.

tool-range.description: What a machine can do along one property: a range, not a value. A bare number is a fixed value, [min, max] a range, and [min, max, default] a range with the value the machine uses when nothing asks for one.

tool-retraction.description: What the machine pulls the material back by when it stops putting it down, so it does not string across the gap to where it prints next. A property of the extruder rather than of the part - a Bowden tube needs several millimeters where a direct drive needs a fraction of one. Declaring this section is the capability: a machine that says nothing here is one nothing is retracted on.

distance.description: How much material to pull back, in millimeters of filament. Without it nothing is retracted, whatever else the section says.

feedRate.description: How fast to pull it back, in mm/min.

zHop.description: How far to lift the tool while travelling with the material pulled back, in millimeters. Zero, or absent, travels at printing height.

minTravel.description: The shortest travel worth retracting for, in millimeters. A hop shorter than this strings less than the retraction itself costs.

tool-positioning.description: What the machine has to be told before it can put anything down: the sequence that gets the tool to a known point over the bed, which is what a CAM plugin turns into the preamble of the file it writes. Named for what each one is rather than for the G-code that carries it.

absolute.description: Absolute coordinates rather than relative ones.

home.description: The axes to home, in the order they are homed in. An empty list means the machine is already referenced and must not be homed.

safeZ.description: How far above the bed the tool travels, in millimeters.

origin.description: Where the tool starts, as [x, y, z] in millimeters.

prime.description: The purge line the machine draws before the first layer.

tool-visual.description: The part that stands for this tool in a picture. Only ever a likeness: it is never manufactured, never ordered and never counted, so the part it names does not have to be manufacturable.

tool-visual-short-form.description: The short form of a tool: the part that stands for it. A tool with nothing else to say about itself - a finger has no torque rating - is written this way.

connect.description: What this part or assembly contributes to every connection it takes part in. The defaults for the 'how' section of an ASSY 'connect*' node.

parameter-override.description: One value of an object's 'with:'. A string may not contain ',', ';' or '=': overriding an object's parameters asks for the instance of it that has those values, and the name of that instance is spelled '<name>;<parameter>=<value>,...' - the same name 'pc inspect cube;width=20.0' asks for. Those three characters are what that spelling is made of, so a value carrying one of them cannot be named.

parameter-default.description: What a parameter is worth when nothing overrides it, and what its 'enum' offers. The same naming constraint as '#/definitions/parameter-override' applies to a string, for the same reason: a value that cannot be spelled in an instance name cannot be asked for by name. Any other type is left alone - only strings carry those characters.

cam.description: The 'cam:' section: the manufacturing instructions 'pc cam' writes. Not a file another tool opens as geometry and not a document about the part, but a program for one machine, correct only for that machine - which is why PartCAD ships no implementation of it and every file type here comes from a package that knows a machine.

cam-output-type.description: One kind of manufacturing instructions. Every field of an output type, plus the one thing that is only meaningful here.

visual.description: What the implementation's picture of these instructions is written as - the file type its 'process_visual(path, request)' entry point produces, which is a 3D model of what the instructions do rather than of the part. Absent where the implementation draws nothing; 'true' means the default, STL. Produced by 'pc cam --visual' and shown in the editor's CAM tab.

render.description: The 'render:' section: the 2D projections and documents 'pc render' writes. Its file types are open-ended, like every output section, but the raster options of the built-in formats are still checked.

raster-output-type.description: A rasterized projection. Only what the built-in rasterizers understand is typed here; a package that replaces the implementation may add parameters of its own, which is why this does not close the object.

pythonVersion.description: The interpreter this package's sandboxes are built on. Defaults to the one PartCAD pins, not to the one PartCAD is running on, so a package renders on the same Python for everyone who opens it. A version newer than the CAD packages PartCAD pins are built for is held down to the newest that has wheels, and says so.

suppliers.description: The providers to consider for the parts and assemblies of this package. A name is a provider of this package unless it is qualified with a package path, which lets a package buy from a provider defined elsewhere.

manufacturing.description: How this part is made. 'method' is the kind of process; everything else is what that process has to be told. Only 'additive' takes settings so far, and each of them is a value the machine named by 'tool' has a range for.

tool.description: The machine that makes this part: a reference to a tool of the matching category - an 'additive' tool for an additive part.

material.description: What the machine is loaded with. Defaults to 'properties.material', which is what the finished part is made of; the two come apart when a part is printed in whatever is on the spool and painted afterwards.

color.description: The colour it is made in. Defaults to 'properties.color'.

temperature.description: In degrees Celsius, at the tool.

bedTemperature.description: In degrees Celsius, at the bed.

oneOf.description: A part built by a package-defined partType (its 'type' references a partType). partType-specific properties are allowed.

precision.description: The number of decimal places the placement of each component is rounded to ('step' type only)

ignoreCollision.description: Build a URDF link from its visual geometry rather than its collision geometry: true for every link, or a list of the link names it applies to ('urdf' type only)

packagePaths.description: Roots to resolve 'package://' mesh references against ('urdf' type only)

strict.description: Fail on a Gazebo setting that has no PartCAD property, instead of reporting it. URDF outside Gazebo's extension blocks always fails, whatever this says ('urdf' type only)

scenes.description: Scenes: placed arrangements of objects - a workcell, a table, a simulation world - stating where things are and not how they got there. Declared by pointing at the file that holds one, with no assembly object in between

type.description: 'assy' is an Assembly YAML file read as a scene, which is the same format without the 'how' sections; 'world' is a Gazebo world (SDFormat) file

ignoreCollision.description: Build a link from its visual geometry rather than its collision geometry: true for every link, or a list of the link names it applies to ('world' type only)

modelPaths.description: Roots to resolve 'model://' references against ('world' type only)

manufacturable.description: A scene is not a product to be made, so it is not manufacturable unless it says so

threadStep.description: The axial distance a connection made through this interface advances per full turn, in mm. Inherited by the interfaces that inherit this one, and by the connections that use it.

selfScrew.description: Whether this interface cuts its own thread rather than matching one, so that it may be connected to an interface with a different 'threadStep' or none.

software.description: The software this package ships: firmware images, binaries, disk images. Software is an object of a package like a part is, and unlike a part it has no geometry - it is always a file. Every type is a file; the types beyond 'raw' will name the firmware flashing procedure the file goes through (which tool, which bootloader), never a different way of pointing at it.

oneOf.description: The short form: the path of the file, relative to the package.

type.description: 'raw' is the file handed over as it is, and is the default.

fileHash.description: As elsewhere. Software is the one place a missing one is reported before anything is built: see the 'Software' lint check.

tools.description: The tools this package declares: what a product is made *with* rather than of - a finger, a driver, an extruder, an end mill. Unlike every other section, this one does not enumerate its objects: it holds one sub-section per category, and the sub-section name becomes the 'category' property of every tool declared inside it. The category also decides what a tool may say about itself, because each of them is a class of its own.

mechanical.description: Tools that hold, turn or press something. The one category an assembly step may name in its 'how' section (see docs/source/assy.rst).

mates.description: The interface, or the list of interfaces, this tool meets an object through. It is what lets an assembly step ask to be held by this tool and say nothing else: every instance of these interfaces the object implements is then a place the tool fits.

forceMin.description: The least force this tool can usefully apply, in newtons (N).

forceMax.description: The most force this tool can apply, in newtons (N).

torqueMax.description: The most torque this tool can apply, in newton-metres (N*m). A tool that cannot turn what it holds leaves this at zero, which is what disqualifies it from being a connection's 'driver'.

additive.description: Tools that put material down: an extruder, a laser sintering a bed.

process.description: How the material is put down: 'fdm', 'sla', 'sls', 'dmls', and whatever else a package needs to name.

materials.description: What this machine can put down. 'material' in the singular is the one-entry form.

buildVolume.description: How much fits, as [x, y, z] in millimeters.

stepSize.description: The smallest move the machine can make on each axis, as [x, y, z] in millimeters: the resolution of its motion system, which is what says whether a feature is reachable at all.

layerHeight.description: The thickness of one layer, in millimeters.

spotSize.description: The width of what the tool lays down in one pass, in millimeters: a nozzle bore, a laser spot.

speed.description: How fast it puts material down, in mm/s.

temperature.description: At the tool, in degrees Celsius.

bedTemperature.description: At the bed, in degrees Celsius.

subtractive.description: Tools that take material away: an end mill, a drill, a laser cutting.

process.description: How the material is taken away: 'milling', 'turning', 'drilling', 'laser', 'waterjet', 'edm', and whatever else a package needs to name.

length.description: The usable cutting length, in millimeters.

flutes.description: How many cutting edges the tool has.

spindleSpeedMax.description: The most the tool may be turned at, in rpm.

feedRateMax.description: The most the tool may be fed at, in mm/min.
